title: Smazeny Syr
subtitle: Czech fried cheese
excerpt: Thick slices of cheese are double-coated in egg and breadcrumbs and deep-fried until golden. Smazeny syr is a Czech fast-food icon -- sold at street windows and pub menus across the country. Simple, satisfying, and very quick to make.
sourceNotes: Smazeny syr is a Czech fast-food icon. A thick slice of cheese is coated in breadcrumbs and fried until golden. It is sold at Czech fast-food windows and in pubs nationwide. Edam or Hermelin (a camembert-style cheese) are traditional.

content.text: The double coating -- egg, breadcrumbs, egg, breadcrumbs again -- is non-negotiable. A single coat leaves gaps and the cheese will escape into the oil. Keep the oil at 170°C and the cheese will be golden outside and just melted within.

items.prepNote: use Edam or Hermelin if available -- cut into 2 thick slices, each about 1.5cm

content.text: Cut cheese into 2 thick slices about 1.5cm each. Season the flour with salt.
Coat each slice in seasoned flour, shaking off excess. Dip in beaten egg. Press into breadcrumbs until fully coated with no gaps.
Dip in egg again, then breadcrumbs a second time for extra security. Check for any bare patches and patch them.
Heat oil in a pan to 170°C. Fry each slice for 2-3 minutes per side until deep golden. Drain on kitchen paper.
Serve immediately with mayonnaise and chips or a simple salad.

items.cause: Breading has gaps or oil too hot
items.fix: Double-coat in egg and breadcrumbs and check for bare patches. Keep oil at 170°C.

content.text: Czech Republic. One of the country's most beloved fast foods. Found at street-food windows called bufet across Prague and other cities. Often eaten on the go with tartare sauce or mayonnaise.
